## Context

Deferred non-blocking advisories from the change-triggered criterion-eval work (ticket 5169,
epic R-4 `spin-cub-usher` / 65dd-e93b-666a-4caa). Each was dispositioned defer-followup: all
are non-blocking, LLM-Review+1 was granted, the `eval-changed-rubrics` job is
continue-on-error, and CI itself uses ANTHROPIC/OPENAI credentials so the gating is correct
for CI today. They matter for portability (non-CI / Bedrock-only environments) and test
coverage, so they are collected here rather than dropped.

## Scope

`src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py` (the live criteria-eval availability check and the
change-triggered run loop) and its unit tests.

## Deferred items to disposition

- [ ] `_live_criteria_eval_available` gates on ANTHROPIC/OPENAI env only; a Bedrock repo
      model with Bedrock creds is seen as "no live", so a Bedrock-only environment silently
      skips the live half.
- [ ] Fail-open: when live is available but every criterion raises LLMError, the run returns
      None and the caller exits 0 unconditionally, even under `--require-live`.
- [ ] Empty `--changed-since ''` is not treated as a null ref; it falls through to the
      missing-criterion error (exit 2) instead of a clean no-op.
- [ ] The per-criterion LLMError recovery path in the live-run loop has no test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each item above is either fixed (with a covering test where it is a correctness or
      coverage gap) or explicitly accepted with a one-line reason recorded on this ticket.
      In particular, decide whether `--require-live` must fail non-zero when live was
      available but produced no successful evaluation.

## Budget

To be estimated when claimed.

## Root Cause

Current `rebar criteria eval --changed-since` fixed several R-4 review findings, but the deferred follow-ups are still real on current main. `_live_criteria_eval_available` only treats Anthropic/OpenAI API-key env vars as live, so a Bedrock-configured repo with AWS ambient credentials is reported as no-live. `_run_selected_criteria_live` catches every per-criterion `LLMError` and returns no success/failure summary, so `_criteria_eval_changed_since` exits 0 whenever live was considered available, even if every selected criterion failed under `--require-live`. `_is_null_ref` recognizes all-zero SHAs but not an explicitly empty `--changed-since ''`, so that input reaches the missing-criterion/error path instead of the same clean first-push/no-baseline no-op. The per-criterion `LLMError` branch is also behaviorally unpinned.

## Plan

- Add unit tests for the remaining live changed-criteria edge cases: Bedrock provider-identity availability (not credential usability), `--require-live` failing non-zero when all selected live criteria raise `LLMError`, empty `--changed-since ''` returning the null-ref no-op, and mixed live runs continuing after one criterion-level `LLMError` while reporting that failure.
- Update `_live_criteria_eval_available` to recognize Bedrock by provider identity only: when the agents runtime is installed and `LLMConfig.from_env()` plus `resolve_model`/`infer_provider` resolves the configured model provider to `bedrock`. This does not cheaply prove AWS credential usability; a Bedrock-configured but uncredentialed environment is intentionally allowed to attempt live execution, and the new `--require-live` zero-success failure is the safety net that makes that misconfiguration red instead of a silent green skip.
- Have the live selected-criteria loop return a success count so `--require-live` can fail when live execution was attempted but produced zero successful evaluations.
- Distinguish a present `--changed-since` flag from an absent one by checking `args.changed_since is not None` in the dispatcher and mutual-exclusion guard, then treat the present-but-empty value as a null/no-baseline ref in `_is_null_ref`.

## Testing

- RED: run the new targeted tests first and confirm they fail on current main.
- GREEN: run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_changed_criteria.py -q`.
- Run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`.
- Before push, run `env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT -u GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 -u GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1 -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1 -u GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2 -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2 PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make verify`.
